clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old boy presented with an 11-month history of recurrent diarrhea and weight loss. On examination, he had bilateral pitting edema of the lower limbs, indicating protein loss. Initial laboratory investigation revealed hypoalbuminemia and lymphopenia. CT abdomen showed circumferential jejunal thickening, islands of echogenic fat in the mesentery, enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes, and minimal pelvic ascites—findings consistent with lymphatic obstruction and protein-losing enteropathy. Upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsy was performed, and histopathologic examination confirmed the diagnosis of duodenal lymphangiectasia, demonstrating intact columnar lining with blunted villi, dilated lymphatic channels containing proteinaceous fluid within the lumen, and moderate lymphoplasmacytic infiltration in the lamina propria. Following diagnosis confirmation, the patient was treated with a high-protein diet and medium-chain triglycerides (replacing long-chain triglycerides). On reassessment during regular hospital follow-up, there was gradual improvement in symptoms.
